facts.fact: GabonReview reports that an inter-ministerial workshop opened at Ntoum on 28 September 2026, to run to 8 October, to prepare the national civil registration conferences and define the conditions for putting the Centre national d'état civil (CNEC) into operation.

The Gabon Digital general coordinator is reported as saying the workshop's recommendations should lead to decisions breaking with the current manual procedures of civil registration; no office count is given.

The Gabon Digital general coordinator is reported as saying the rules for attributing identity will be transposed into a platform only once the decisions are taken, the digital platforms for managing civil registration coming second; no digital registration of births or deaths is described as in service.
GabonReview states the Gabon Digital programme, whose component 2 carries the Centre national d'état civil, is financed by the World Bank.

GabonReview states the Gabon Digital programme is steered by the Ministry of the Digital Economy through a steering committee and a technical committee with the administrations concerned; the workshop was opened by the secretary-general of the Ministry of the Interior, Security and Decentralisation.

GabonReview states the civil registration reform is among the priorities of the Plan national de croissance et de développement (PNCD) 2026-2030, and that the Digital Gabon project provides for the digitisation of civil registration; the article does not say the plan names the CNEC.
